newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Junior Czech govt party reluctantly backs budget.
newsitem.headline: Junior Czech govt party reluctantly backs budget.

text.p: The Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), a junior member of the Czech coalition government, said on Wednesday it would support the state budget in the first parliamentary reading but only with reservations.
The opposition far-right Republicans told parliament that they would vote against the 1997 budget. The voting is due later on Wednesday at the earliest.
Senior ODA deputy Pavel Ledvinka gave only qualified support to the draft budget, which is likely to face a vote on its first reading later on Wednesday.

"The ODA accepts the budget as a member of the coalition with many objections because it diverges from the profile of the government which we participated in. We will support it in the first reading," he told the budget debate.

Earlier, the ODA's parliamentary leader Ivan Masek said the budget did not go far enough in cutting taxes and did not have an anti-inflationary effect because it was merely balanced and did not run a surplus.
The Communists said earlier on Wednesday that they would vote against the budget but the main opposition party, the Social Democrats, appear split.

Social Democrat leader Milos Zeman has called for changes to the budget but his party colleague Jozef Wagner, the chairman of the parliamentary budget committee, has called for the budget to be approved for the sake of economic stability.
The government holds 99 out of 200 seats in parliament and therefore needs only two opposition defections to win.
